questions.question: What is Anycast routing?

options.text: Routing to any available server randomly
Multiple servers sharing the same IP address, with traffic routed to the nearest one

questions.explanation: Anycast assigns the same IP address to multiple servers in different locations. BGP routing directs traffic to the topologically nearest server. Used by CDNs and DNS services for low-latency global distribution.

questions.question: Which services commonly use Anycast routing? (Choose all that apply)
questions.explanation: CDNs use Anycast to route users to nearest edge. DNS root servers use it for resilience and performance. DDoS mitigation uses it to absorb attacks across distributed scrubbing centers. Traditional apps typically use unicast.

questions.question: How does Anycast differ from GeoDNS for global load distribution?

options.text: Anycast routes at network layer (BGP); GeoDNS routes at application layer (DNS)

questions.explanation: Anycast uses BGP routing—the network itself directs packets to the nearest server. GeoDNS returns different IPs based on client location. Anycast is transparent to clients; GeoDNS requires DNS resolution.

questions.question: What is a key advantage of Anycast for DDoS mitigation?

options.text: Attack traffic is distributed across multiple locations, preventing single-point overload
It blocks all malicious IPs automatically
It makes servers invisible to attackers

questions.explanation: Anycast distributes attack traffic across all locations advertising the IP. No single location bears the full attack load. Combined with scrubbing at each location, this provides effective DDoS absorption.

questions.question: Why is Anycast particularly well-suited for UDP-based services like DNS?

options.text: UDP is connectionless, so routing changes don't break sessions

questions.explanation: UDP is stateless—each packet is independent. If routing changes mid-session, UDP continues working. TCP connections would break if packets suddenly route to a different server mid-connection.

questions.question: What challenge does Anycast present for TCP-based services?

options.text: Routing changes can cause TCP connections to fail
TCP is too slow for Anycast

questions.explanation: TCP is stateful. If BGP routing changes during a connection, subsequent packets may route to a different server that doesn't have the connection state, causing connection reset. Stable routing is important.

questions.question: True or False: With Anycast, clients explicitly choose which server to connect to.
questions.explanation: Anycast is transparent to clients. They connect to a single IP address; the network (BGP routing) determines which physical server receives the traffic based on network topology and routing policies.

questions.question: A CDN uses Anycast with servers in 50 locations. A server in Tokyo fails. What happens to traffic that was going to Tokyo?

options.text: Traffic is lost until manual intervention
BGP withdraws the route; traffic automatically reroutes to the next nearest server

questions.explanation: When a server fails, it stops advertising the Anycast IP via BGP. Traffic automatically reroutes to the next nearest location advertising that IP. This provides automatic failover at the network layer.

questions.question: What is required to implement Anycast?

options.text: Control over BGP routing (typically requires owning IP space and AS number)

questions.explanation: Anycast requires advertising the same IP prefix from multiple locations via BGP. This typically requires owning IP address space, an AS number, and peering arrangements—usually only feasible for large organizations or cloud providers.

questions.question: How does Cloudflare's 1.1.1.1 DNS service achieve global low latency?

options.text: Anycast routing to hundreds of global locations

questions.explanation: Cloudflare uses Anycast—1.1.1.1 is advertised from 200+ locations worldwide. Users automatically connect to the nearest location, minimizing latency. The same IP works globally but resolves locally.

questions.question: Which statement about Anycast and unicast is correct?

options.text: Unicast sends to multiple destinations; Anycast sends to one
Anycast: one IP, multiple destinations (nearest wins); Unicast: one IP, one destination
Anycast is deprecated in favor of unicast

questions.explanation: Unicast: one-to-one (each IP maps to one destination). Anycast: one-to-nearest (same IP on multiple servers, routing picks nearest). Broadcast: one-to-all. Multicast: one-to-many (subscribed group).

questions.question: A company wants to use Anycast but doesn't own IP space. What is their best option?

options.text: Anycast is impossible without owned IP space
Use a CDN or cloud provider that offers Anycast as a service

questions.explanation: CDNs (Cloudflare, Akamai) and cloud providers (AWS Global Accelerator) offer Anycast as a managed service. Customers get Anycast benefits without managing BGP, IP space, or global infrastructure.
